companies.name: Western Wildfire
companies.summary: Certified design, installation and testing of Ember Armor exterior sprinkler kits, including custom water-source solutions, fire hose and copper line runs, and remote activation. Quotes are turned around within a day from property photos.
companies.priceNote: Base home installation from $699.99 CAD; sized to budget
companies.verified: Verified from the company's own site, September 2026

companies.name: Prodigy Wildfire Solutions
companies.summary: Permanent exterior wildfire sprinkler systems using roof-mounted nozzles to build a humidity barrier around the structure. Systems are installed in a single day and the BC offering is described as FireSmart-compliant.
companies.verified: Verified from the company's own site, September 2026

companies.name: SPIEDR
companies.summary: Manufacturer of structure protection units and sprinkler trailers — by their own account 98% of those bought in Canada — plus WATERAX-powered pumps, wildfire consulting, rentals and certified training. Their market is municipalities, resorts, wineries and industry rather than individual homes.
companies.verified: Verified from the company's own site, September 2026. Note: not a homeowner installer — listed for acreage, strata and community-scale projects.

companies.name: Flash Wildfire Services
companies.summary: Canadian supplier of wildfire defence equipment: WATERAX portable pumps, sprinkler kits, fire hose, nozzles, hand tools and protective gear, plus custom-built trailers and skid units. Ships nationally.
companies.verified: Verified from the company's own site, September 2026. Supply rather than installation.

companies.name: WASP Wildfire Protection Products
companies.summary: Canadian-made gutter-clip sprinkler heads and complete wildfire protection kits that install without tools and run from a garden hose. Widely stocked by Canadian retailers.
companies.priceNote: Kits vary by number of heads
companies.verified: Verified from the company's own site, September 2026. Supply rather than installation.

programs.name: Wildfire Mitigation Program — free certified home assessment
programs.note: A certified professional assesses your property and gives wildfire-protection recommendations at no cost. Book through the interactive map.

programs.name: FireSmart BC Coordinators
programs.note: Local coordinators run neighbourhood assessments and community FireSmart activity in most regional districts.

programs.name: TNRD FireSmart Homeowner Rebate
programs.note: Thompson-Nicola Regional District reimburses homeowners for qualifying wildfire-resistant upgrades. Check your own regional district too — several run comparable programs.

programs.name: City of Kamloops FireSmart assessments and rebates
programs.note: Free home assessments plus rebates for qualifying work.

programs.name: FireSmart Alberta
programs.note: Provincial coordination of community assessments, the Neighbourhood Recognition Program and local vegetation-management support.

programs.name: RMWB FireSmart Rebate Program
programs.note: The Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo reimburses residents for wildfire-resistant home upgrades.

programs.name: FireSmart Saskatchewan (SPSA)
programs.note: The Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency coordinates FireSmart assessments and planning with northern municipalities.

programs.name: Saskatchewan First Nations Emergency Management — FireSmart
programs.note: FireSmart programming delivered specifically for First Nations communities in Saskatchewan.

programs.name: Manitoba Wildfire Service — FireSmart resources
programs.note: Provincial homeowner resources and FireSmart guidance. Local organising in cottage country runs through municipalities and cottage associations.

programs.name: Ontario Forest Fires (MNR)
programs.note: Fire status, restricted fire zones and community FireSmart programming, concentrated in the northwest.

programs.name: SOPFEU
programs.note: Quebec's forest fire protection agency handles both suppression and prevention, and is the province's FireSmart liaison.

programs.name: NB Fire Watch — Wildfire Management
programs.note: Daily fire weather index, burn restrictions and permit information. Permits are required through much of the season.

programs.name: NS Natural Resources and Renewables — FireSmart
programs.note: Provincial FireSmart programming, substantially expanded since the 2023 Tantallon and Barrington Lake fires.

programs.name: PEI Forests, Fish and Wildlife
programs.note: Provincial fire ban status and forestry contact. PEI maintains a FireSmart liaison.

programs.name: NL Fisheries, Forestry and Agriculture
programs.note: Provincial fire status, bans and prevention guidance. Municipal FireSmart organising has grown since the 2025 Kingston fire.

programs.name: Yukon Wildland Fire Management — FireSmart
programs.note: Offers FireSmart property assessments across the territory, plus fire locations and evacuation alerts.

programs.name: GNWT Environment and Climate Change — FireSmart
programs.note: Territorial FireSmart coordination and community fuel break work, substantially expanded since 2023.

programs.name: No FireSmart program in Nunavut
programs.note: FireSmart Canada confirms there is no active Neighbourhood Recognition Program in the territory. For structural fire safety, contact your hamlet office and the Office of the Fire Marshal.
